title: Gordan lemma for lattice points in a rational cone
statement: Let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, an abelian group with elements $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ such that every element of $L$ is uniquely $\sum_j m_je_j$ with $m_j\in\mathbf Z$; regard $L\subseteq L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in L$, allowing $r=0$. Put $C=\{\sum_i q_i v_i:q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge 0}\}\subseteq L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $P=\{\sum_i n_i v_i:n_i\in\mathbf N\}\subseteq L$. Then there is a finite set $F\subseteq C\cap L$ such that $C\cap L=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$. In particular, $C\cap L$ is a finitely generated commutative monoid, generated by $F$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104 (finite toric saturation); expanded as the standard fundamental-parallelepiped proof of Gordan's lemma.

proof.text: Write $v_i=\sum_{j=1}^d a_{ij}e_j$ with $a_{ij}\in\mathbf Z$. Define $Q=\{\sum_{i=1}^r t_i v_i:t_i\in\mathbf Q,\ 0\le t_i<1\}$ and $B_j=\sum_{i=1}^r|a_{ij}|$. The $j$th coordinate of a point of $Q$ is $\sum_i t_i a_{ij}$, whose absolute value is at most $B_j$. Consequently the basis-coordinate map injects $Q\cap L$ into the finite product $\prod_{j=1}^d([-B_j,B_j]\cap\mathbf Z)$. Set $F=Q\cap L$; it is finite and contained in $C\cap L$, since all the coefficients defining $Q$ are rational and nonnegative. Empty products and sums give $F=\{0\}$ when $d=0$ or $r=0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104, finite toric saturation assertion; agent expansion, step 1 of the elementary lattice-coordinate proof.

proof.text: Given $x\in C\cap L$, write $x=\sum_i q_i v_i$ with $q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$. Set $n_i=\lfloor q_i\rfloor\in\mathbf N$ and $t_i=q_i-n_i\in\mathbf Q\cap[0,1)$. Then $p=\sum_i n_i v_i\in P$ and $f=\sum_i t_i v_i=x-p$ belongs to $Q$ and to $L$; thus $f\in F$ and $x=f+p$. This proves $C\cap L\subseteq\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$. Conversely, write $f\in F\subseteq C\cap L$ and $p\in P\subseteq C\cap L$ as nonnegative rational combinations of the $v_i$. Adding their coefficients shows $f+p\in C$; as both summands lie in $L$, $f+p\in C\cap L$. Hence $C\cap L=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104, finite toric saturation assertion; agent expansion, step 2 of the elementary lattice-coordinate proof.

proof.text: The displayed equality gives finite generation. Every element of $C\cap L$ is a sum of one element of the finite set $F$ and elements of $P$, while $P$ is generated by $v_1,\ldots,v_r$. Conversely, each $f\in F$ and each $v_i$ belongs to $C\cap L$. Therefore the commutative monoid $C\cap L$ is generated by $F$ together with $v_1,\ldots,v_r$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104, finite toric saturation assertion; agent expansion, step 3 of the elementary lattice-coordinate proof.

lean.statement: theorem gordan_rational_cone_finite (L : Type u) [AddCommGroup L] [Module ℤ L] [Module.Free ℤ L] [Module.Finite ℤ L] (r : ℕ) (v : Fin r → L) : let ι : L → TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ := fun x => TensorProduct.mk ℤ L ℚ x 1 let C : Set (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ) := {x | ∃ q : Fin r → ℚ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ q i) ∧ x = ∑ i, TensorProduct.mk ℤ L ℚ (v i) (q i)} let P : Set (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ) := {x | ∃ n : Fin r → ℕ, x = ∑ i, TensorProduct.mk ℤ L ℚ (v i) (n i : ℚ)} let Lset : Set (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ) := Set.range ι ∃ F : Finset (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ), (∀ f ∈ F, f ∈ C ∩ Lset) ∧ C ∩ Lset = ⋃ f ∈ (F : Set (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ)), {x | ∃ p ∈ P, x = f + p} ∧ AddSubmonoid.closure ((F : Set (TensorProduct ℤ L ℚ)) ∪ Set.range (fun i => ι (v i))) = C ∩ Lset
